title: Lesson 8 · Prepositions & Phrases
blurb: Prepositions, prepositional phrases, adjective vs adverbial phrases, infinitives, and misplaced modifiers.

items.prompt:
Which word is the preposition?

“The boy went through the gate.”
items.explain: “through” shows the relation of “gate” to “went” — the preposition.

items.prompt:
Which word is the preposition?

“He drove over the bridge.”
items.explain: “over” shows the relation of “bridge” to “drove” — the preposition.

items.prompt:
Which word is the preposition?

“She went to the doctor.”
items.explain: “to” shows the relation of “doctor” to “went” — the preposition.

items.prompt:
Which word is the preposition?

“He sat beside the fire.”
items.explain: “beside” shows where he sat in relation to the fire — the preposition.

items.prompt:
Which word is the preposition?

“They walked into the garden.”
items.explain: “into” shows the relation of “garden” to “walked” — the preposition.

items.prompt:
Which word is the preposition?

“Put the book on the shelf.”
items.explain: “on” shows the relation of “shelf” to “Put” — the preposition.

items.prompt:
Which word is the preposition?

“The dog slept under the porch.”
items.explain: “under” shows the relation of “porch” to “slept” — the preposition.

items.prompt:
Which word is the preposition?

“We walked across the field.”
items.explain: “across” shows the relation of “field” to “walked” — the preposition.

items.prompt:
Which words make the prepositional phrase?

“The book on the table is mine.”
items.explain: “on the table” is the preposition “on” with its object “table” — the phrase.

items.prompt:
Which words make the prepositional phrase?

“He ran to the store.”
items.explain: “to the store” is the preposition with its object — the phrase.

items.prompt:
Which words make the prepositional phrase?

“A man of wealth arrived.”
items.explain: “of wealth” is the preposition “of” with its object — the phrase.

items.prompt:
Which words make the prepositional phrase?

“She sang with great joy.”
items.explain: “with great joy” is the preposition “with” and its object — the phrase.

items.prompt:
Which words make the prepositional phrase?

“The dog slept under the porch.”
items.explain: “under the porch” is the preposition with its object — the phrase.

items.prompt:
Which words make the prepositional phrase?

“We walked through the woods.”
items.explain: “through the woods” is the preposition with its object — the phrase.

items.prompt:
Does the phrase modify a noun (adjective) or a verb (adverbial)?

“The house on the hill is old.”
items.explain: “on the hill” tells which house — an adjective phrase.

items.prompt:
Does the phrase modify a noun (adjective) or a verb (adverbial)?

“He walked to school.”
items.explain: “to school” tells where he walked — an adverbial phrase.

items.prompt:
Does the phrase modify a noun (adjective) or a verb (adverbial)?

“A book of poems fell.”
items.explain: “of poems” tells which book — an adjective phrase.

items.prompt:
Does the phrase modify a noun (adjective) or a verb (adverbial)?

“She sang in the choir.”
items.explain: “in the choir” tells where she sang — an adverbial phrase.

items.prompt:
Does the phrase modify a noun (adjective) or a verb (adverbial)?

“The man with the hat left.”
items.explain: “with the hat” tells which man — an adjective phrase.

items.prompt:
Does the phrase modify a noun (adjective) or a verb (adverbial)?

“They played in the yard.”
items.explain: “in the yard” tells where they played — an adverbial phrase.

items.prompt:

items.explain: “To lie” is “to” plus the verb — the infinitive.

items.prompt:
What is the infinitive doing — subject, object, or telling why?

“To lie is wicked.”
items.explain: “To lie” is what the sentence is about — the subject.

items.prompt:
What is the infinitive doing — subject, object, or telling why?

“He wants to go home.”
items.explain: “to go home” is what he wants — the object.

items.prompt:

items.prompt:
The modifier is out of place, so the sentence sounds silly. What does it seem to describe?

“I saw a man walking a dog with a hat.”
items.explain: “with a hat” sits next to “dog,” so it seems the dog wears the hat.
